If this PR is red because Renovate could not relock, run `uv lock` and commit `uv.lock` here. --- ### Release Notes
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest) ### [`v9.2.0`](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.2.0) [Compare Source](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.1.1...9.2.0) ##### pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27) ##### Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes - [#​14716](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14716): `-c` now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled `FileNotFoundError`. - [#​8593](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8593): The `indirect`, `ids` and `scope` arguments of `Metafunc.parametrize() ` -- and therefore of `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` -- are now keyword-only. Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. `parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)])` made the argvalues land in `indirect` and failed with `indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist`; such mistakes now fail with an understandable `TypeError`. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only. - [#​993](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/993): Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code `1`: - a plugin that cannot be found -- via `-p`, `pytest_plugins` or `PYTEST_PLUGINS` -- exits with `pytest.ExitCode` `USAGE_ERROR` (`4`), like a `conftest.py` that fails to import; - a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken `pytest11` entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with `pytest.ExitCode` `INTERNAL_ERROR` (`3`), with the traceback preserved. `pytest.main` now returns these codes instead of raising `ImportError`. Also fixed an `IndexError` from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments. ##### Deprecations (removal in next major release) - [#​14742](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14742): The private `_pytest.python.CallSpec2` name has been renamed to `CallSpec`. The old `CallSpec2` alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11. - [#​14755](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14755): Schedule *yield_fixture* decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11. - [#​14774](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14774): Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, *all* higher-scoped fixtures (`module`, `package`, and `session`) defined as instance methods are now deprecated. They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see `10819` and `14011`. - [#​14808](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14808): Passing a non-string value to a `string`-typed ini option now emits a `pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning`. This affects `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml`. In pytest 10 this will raise a `TypeError`, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path. - [#​7323](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7323): Passing `bytes` to `TerminalReporter.write_line()` is now deprecated, pass a `str` instead. ##### New features - [#​14743](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14743): Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output. - [#​2781](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2781): When `strict_markers` is enabled, marker names used in `-m` expressions are now validated against registered markers. - [#​6881](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6881): Added the `parametrize_long_str_id_strategy` configuration option to control how long `str`/`bytes` parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via `ids=[...]` or `pytest.param(..., id=...)` are not affected. Available strategies: `short` (default, values over 100 chars fall back to `argname+index`), `sha256` (SHA-256 hex digest), `legacy` (keep full value), and `disallow` (error requesting explicit IDs). ##### Improvements in existing functionality - [#​10745](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745): A `RecursionError` whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass `--full-trace` to see every frame. - [#​10745](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745): The line numbers of a module's statements are now computed once per traceback instead of once per traceback entry, which noticeably speeds up rendering failures raised from large test modules. - [#​11418](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11418): The cached rewritten modules in `__pycache__` are now invalidated by a hash of the source instead of its modification time, using the checked-hash pyc format from `552`. Timestamps make the cache useless wherever source files get fresh modification times, most notably in CI: a checkout gives every file a new mtime, so a restored cache is discarded in full and every test module is rewritten again. Hashing the source costs roughly 15 microseconds per file and makes the cache survive that. Existing timestamp based caches are ignored and rewritten once. - [#​12624](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12624): The `pytest_plugins` variable and the `PYTEST_PLUGINS` environment variable now also accept entry point names of installed plugins (e.g. `xdist`), in addition to importable module names, matching the behavior of the `-p` command-line option. As part of this change, plugins specified by entry point name through these mechanisms are now also listed in the `plugins:` line of the terminal header (`12615`). Based on the original implementation by Marcel Telka in `12616`. - [#​12697](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12697): Warnings emitted while importing plugins through `-p`, `PYTEST_PLUGINS`, or entry point autoloading are now captured, filtered, and reported like other warnings. - [#​12860](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12860): Assertion diffs for `dict.items()` and `dict.keys()` comparisons (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `==`) now show which items are missing, the same way set comparisons do. - [#​13354](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13354): `Node.get_closest_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.get_closest_marker>` now also accepts a `~pytest.MarkDecorator` as its `default`, for example `item.get_closest_marker("foo", pytest.mark.foo(1))`, and returns the wrapped `~pytest.Mark`. Previously the only way to build a `default` was to instantiate `~pytest.Mark` directly, which is private and warns. - [#​13369](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13369): Improved the error from `pytest.RunResult.assert_outcomes` when a plugin changes or removes pytest's standard terminal summary, and documented how to isolate output-changing plugins. - [#​13431](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13431): Exposed `pytest.ParameterSet` as the type of the return value of `pytest.param()`. This can be used in type annotations and `isinstance` checks. - [#​13564](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13564): Issue a warning when fixtures are wrapped with a decorator that prevents correct discovery, including `@classmethod` above `@pytest.fixture` and `@staticmethod` above `@pytest.fixture`. Put `@pytest.fixture` above those decorators on test classes. - [#​14164](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14164): Exposed `pytest.Approx` as the type of the return value of `pytest.approx()`. This can be used in type annotations and `isinstance` checks. - [#​14463](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14463): Assertion diffs for mappings now match up keys the way the compared mappings match them themselves. Key comparison goes through the mappings' key views instead of plain sets of their keys, so a mapping with its own notion of key equivalence, such as case-insensitive header mappings, no longer reports its common keys as missing on either side. - [#​14523](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14523): Large assertion comparison diffs are now built lazily and capped to the truncation budget, so a huge diff is no longer formatted in full just to be truncated. As a consequence, the truncation footer no longer reports the exact number of hidden lines. - [#​14687](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14687): The default fd-level output capturing (`--capture=fd`) now skips reading the capture buffer for tests which produce no output, reducing per-test overhead in large test suites. - [#​14724](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14724): `--no-summary` now only applies directly to pytest's own summary. The flag no longer skips the `pytest_terminal_summary` hook, so third-party plugins (for example coverage) can still write their terminal summaries. - [#​14751](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14751): `parser.addini ` now also accepts type expressions for its `type` argument, in addition to the existing string tags: the plain Python types `str`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, a `Literal` of strings, and unions of these (for example `int | str` or `int | Literal["auto"]`). - [#​14754](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14754): `pytest.approx()` now rejects infinite relative tolerances for `datetime.timedelta` values with a clear `ValueError` instead of raising `OverflowError`. - [#​14791](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14791): The `junit_family`, `junit_logging`, `junit_duration_report`, `console_output_style`, `empty_parameter_set_mark`, `assertion_text_diff_style` and `tmp_path_retention_policy` configuration options are now registered with the set of values they accept: an invalid value now fails with a clean usage error instead of being silently ignored or crashing later, and `pytest --help` lists the accepted values. `config.getini ` now raises `pytest.UsageError` instead of `TypeError` or `ValueError` when the value read from the configuration file does not match the registered type, so a bad value is always reported as a short usage error message instead of an internal error traceback. Asking for an option name that was never registered still raises `ValueError`. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): `pytest.approx` now emits `pytest.PytestApproxDecimalToleranceWarning` when a `rel` or `abs` tolerance is given as a `float` that cannot be represented exactly for a `~decimal.Decimal` comparison, since such a tolerance is widened to the float's exact binary value. - [#​14675](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14675), [#​14953](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14953), [#​15153](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15153), [#​15132](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15132): The `truncation_limit_lines`, `truncation_limit_chars`, `max_warnings`, `verbosity_assertions`, `verbosity_test_cases`, `verbosity_subtests`, `tmp_path_retention_count`, `log_level`, `log_cli_level`, `log_file_level`,`log_auto_indent` and `faulthandler_timeout` configuration options now accept native integer (and, for `log_auto_indent`, boolean) values in TOML configuration files, while still accepting strings for backward compatibility. `log_file_mode` now reports invalid values as a usage error. - [#​15254](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15254): `tmp_path` and `TempPathFactory.mktemp ` no longer list the whole base temporary directory on every call, which made sessions with many temporary directories quadratically slow. Numbers are now handed out from a per-prefix counter, skipping names that already exist. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `Node.add_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.add_marker>` now stores a `~pytest.Mark` in `node.keywords`, matching what marks applied during collection store. Previously it stored a `~pytest.MarkDecorator`. - [#​9436](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9436): Avoided formatting tracebacks for tests marked with `xfail(run=False)`. ##### Bug fixes - [#​10128](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10128): Configured warning filters now apply to warnings emitted by `pytest_configure` hooks. - [#​10210](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10210): `pytest.approx` now raises a `TypeError` for any nested container, not only for one of the same type as its parent. Previously `approx([{"k": 1}])` and `approx({"k": [1]})` were accepted and then compared unequal to every value, silently ignoring the tolerance, while `approx([[1]])` correctly reported that nesting is unsupported. - [#​10644](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10644): `monkeypatch.setattr()` no longer leaves a new entry in the instance `__dict__` when it patches an attribute that the instance inherits from its class. Previously `undo()` assigned the inherited value onto the instance, which shadowed the class attribute -- permanently freezing the result for descriptors that resolve dynamically. - [#​1139](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1139): Fixed tracebacks showing `???` instead of source lines for code compiled with a filename relative to a directory other than the current working directory -- e.g. compiled Cython modules, when running pytest from a subdirectory of the project root. The source lookup now falls back to searching `sys.path` for such filenames, as the standard `traceback` module does. - [#​11502](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11502): The `rootdir` is no longer derived from a configuration file that is not a regular file, such as `--config-file=/dev/null`. - [#​11783](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11783): Plugins installed in editable mode (`660`) are marked for assertion rewriting again. Such installs do not record the package's Python files in the distribution metadata, so pytest found nothing to rewrite and assertions inside the plugin lost their introspection. The plugin's entry point is now used to locate the package in that case. - [#​11933](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11933): `pytest.warns` no longer re-emits unmatched warnings with `module="warnings"`, which caused `module`-based warning filters to be applied to the wrong warnings. Since `warnings.WarningMessage` does not record the module a warning was emitted with, re-emitted warnings now use the standard `warnings.warn_explicit` default of deriving the module from the warning's filename. - [#​12175](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12175): `ExceptionInfo.exconly(tryshort=True) ` now strips the `AssertionError:` prefix of failed `assert` statements for `~pytest.ExceptionInfo` objects created by `pytest.raises`, and failures inside `unittest.TestCase.subTest` report the same short crash line as regular tests. - [#​12223](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12223): The `message` attribute of `` and `` elements in `--junitxml` reports is now shortened to whole lines within 500 characters. When something is dropped, it ends with a note pointing to the element text, which still holds the full report. Previously, very verbose assertion output (e.g. with `-vv`) produced attributes tens of thousands of characters long, which some XML parsers fail on. - [#​12307](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12307): Fixed truncation of long collections (lists, dicts, sets, etc.) in the "message" part of failed assertions (as in `assert condition, msg`) when using `-vv`: the message now uses the same unlimited repr as the rest of the assertion output, instead of eliding collection elements with `...`. - [#​12824](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12824): Custom command-line options now fail with a clear error when their implicit destination conflicts with an existing option, avoiding silent overrides of built-in options such as `-k`. - [#​13292](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13292): Fixed a stale rewritten module being used when a test file is modified twice within the same second without changing its size -- the pyc header could only record whole-second timestamps. The cache is now keyed on a hash of the source. - [#​14036](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14036): `__tracebackhide__` is now respected in `ExceptionGroup` tracebacks, both for the group itself and for its sub-exceptions. - [#​14189](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14189): Nested usage of `caplog.filtering ` no longer removes filters early if they were already present. - [#​14412](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14412): Fixed incorrect timing information for subtests and parent tests when `console_output_style = "times"`. - [#​14445](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14445): Assertion rewriting no longer evaluates walrus operator (`:=`) expressions more than once, which reported results the test never computed when the expression had side effects. An operand evaluated before a later walrus is now reported with the value it actually saw, so `assert value != identity(value := value.lower())` keeps Python's left-to-right order. - [#​14552](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14552): Fixed stale `co_filename` values after a test module or directory is moved. Assertion-rewrite caches are reused when the source hash still matches, and in-memory code objects are pointed at the current path. - [#​14586](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14586): Negative values passed to `log_auto_indent` now correctly fall back to no indentation, matching the documented behavior. - [#​14619](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14619): Fixed a crash in `pytest.mark.parametrize` when a non-sequence value is passed for a parameter set. It now provides a clear error message during collection. - [#​14635](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14635): Fixed fixture resolution failures when specifying multiple test paths on the command line that share common parent directories. Parametrized fixtures defined in a `conftest.py` could be silently dropped depending on the order of the specified paths. - [#​14637](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14637): Pytest now correctly skips identical trailing characters in assertion text diffs even when the compared strings differ at the beginning. - [#​14638](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14638): Top-level options in `pytest.toml` and `.pytest.toml` files now raise an error instead of being silently ignored when no `[pytest]` table is present. - [#​14683](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14683): Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1 where a conftest.py located in the rootdir was no longer visible to tests and doctests collected from *outside* the rootdir (for example when passing a parent directory of the rootdir as a collection argument, or setting `--rootdir` to a subdirectory). As a result, fixtures defined in such a conftest -- including `doctest_namespace` injections -- were not available, causing errors such as `NameError` in doctests. - [#​14700](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14700): Fixed an internal error on Python 3.12 when a doctest on a fixture-decorated function was skipped. - [#​14705](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14705): TOML configuration files passed via `-c` now also read their configuration from the `[pytest]` table, the one pytest's own configuration files use. The `[tool.pytest]` and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` tables such files were previously restricted to keep working; using both styles in one file is an error. - [#​14828](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14828): Exception groups raised from another exception now print their cause chain only once in the traceback output. - [#​14864](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14864): Fixed collection on Windows collecting the whole suite instead of the given path, on file systems which do not support file IDs (`st_ino` is `0` for every file, as seen for example on `sshfs-win`/WinFsp mounts). - [#​14884](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14884): `Cache.get()`, `Cache.set()` and `Cache.mkdir()` now reject keys that resolve outside the cache directory, and `--cache-show` ignores glob matches outside it. - [#​14909](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14909): Fixed `MonkeyPatch.delattr `, `MonkeyPatch.setitem ` and `MonkeyPatch.delitem ` recording a stale undo entry when the underlying mutation failed, which could cause spurious errors during teardown. The undo entry is now recorded only after the mutation succeeds, matching the behavior of `MonkeyPatch.setattr `. - [#​14912](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14912): `~pytest.PytestWarning` instances defined in `_pytest.deprecated` are no longer reused across `warnings.warn` calls, so warnings raised as errors (e.g. with `-W error`) no longer accumulate stale traceback frames from previous raises. - [#​14942](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14942): Fixed a regression in 9.1.0 that made collection very slow (quadratic) when many fixtures are defined with the same name. This can happen particularly when many tests are defined in separate classes which inherit from a base class which defines fixtures (the fixtures are repeated per class). - [#​15005](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15005): `pytest.approx` no longer treats finite `~decimal.Decimal` values outside the `float` range (such as `Decimal("1e400")`) as infinite, which made in-tolerance comparisons fail. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): Restored the tolerance shown by `pytest.approx` for `~decimal.Decimal` values, which since 9.0 displayed `???` for the default tolerance and reported the raw `rel` ratio instead of the absolute tolerance actually compared against. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): The failure message for `pytest.approx` comparisons of `~decimal.Decimal` collections no longer reports `Max absolute difference: -inf`, or crashes for mappings, when the `decimal.FloatOperation` trap is set. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): `pytest.approx` no longer raises `AttributeError` when comparing `numpy.ndarray` instances with `object` dtype, such as arrays of `~decimal.Decimal`. - [#​15032](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15032): Help texts for command-line options and configuration options now keep their indentation and blank lines. Previously each line was stripped before wrapping, so a wrapped list item was indistinguishable from a new one and blank lines were dropped; configuration option help lost its line breaks entirely. - [#​15043](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15043): Cache writes now emit `pytest.PytestCacheWarning` when writing or closing the cache file fails, consistent with errors opening the file. - [#​15052](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15052): Fixed possible off-by-one line numbers in `--fixtures` and `--fixtures-per-test` output. - [#​15145](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15145): With `console_output_style` set to `times`, durations just below a unit boundary are now shown in the next unit (e.g. `1.000ms` instead of `1000.0us`). - [#​15172](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15172): Assertion diffs now pretty-print the built-in `frozendict` (Python 3.15+) across multiple lines, similarly to how `dict` is displayed. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `-k` no longer matches attributes that end up in a test function's `__dict__` without being meant as keywords, such as pytest's own `pytestmark` attribute and the bookkeeping left behind by `functools.wraps` and `functools.lru_cache`. - [#​6750](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6750): Fix fixture argument discovery for custom collectors that pass bound methods to `pytest.Function`. - [#​6997](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6997): XFAIL reports from teardown phases now include the phase in the short test summary. - [#​7940](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7940): Fixed cleanup of temporary directories failing when subdirectories have their execute permission removed. - [#​8321](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8321): Fixed exception chains being duplicated in the traceback output when an exception in the chain (`__cause__`/`__context__`) has no traceback of its own, and that exception is itself linked to further exceptions. - [#​8914](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8914): Tests parametrized with higher-than-function scope are now reordered by parameter *value* rather than by parameter *index*, so that items using equal parameter values are grouped together and share a single fixture setup, even when they are parametrized by separate `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` calls. Previously, an expensive higher-scoped fixture could be set up and torn down repeatedly for the same parameter value. Unhashable parameter values (e.g. dicts) keep the previous index-based grouping behavior. As a consequence, the order in which parametrized tests run may change (fixture setup/teardown counts can only decrease, not increase). - [#​9924](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9924): Fixed doctest option flags leaking between docstrings after a failure, skip, or expected failure. ##### Improved documentation - [#​10721](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10721): Replaced `setup.py` usage with `pyproject.toml` in `writing-plugins`. - [#​12658](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12658): Moved the fixture setup and finalizer hooks to the test running hooks section in the reference documentation. - [#​12857](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12857): Documented how `--confcutdir` affects initial `conftest.py` discovery. - [#​14157](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14157): Added the `pytest-flakefighters` plugin to the list of flaky test plugins in `plugins.rst`. Added flaky test papers published on the [Test FLARE](https://test-flare.github.io/) project to the list of flaky papers in `plugins.rst`. - [#​15127](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15127): Added guidance on typing yield fixtures, including annotating fixture functions with their generator type and fixture consumers with the yielded value type. - [#​15242](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15242): The `installation instructions ` and `install-package-with-pip` now show how to install pytest into a virtual environment with venv and pip, uv or virtualenv, and explain the `externally-managed-environment` error. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `pytest --help`, the `-k` reference entry and `select-tests` no longer describe `-k` as a Python expression matched against test names only; `keyword expressions` now shows marker names being matched as well. The examples that looked up a marker use `Node.get_closest_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.get_closest_marker>` rather than `item.keywords`. - [#​9614](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9614): Clarified that `session.items` and `session.testscollected` exclude deselected tests in the `pytest_collection` documentation. ##### Packaging updates and notes for downstreams - [#​11680](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11680): Source archives of arbitrary commits -- the tarballs GitHub serves under `/archive/`, not just the ones for tags -- can now be built into an sdist or a wheel with a correct version. A `.git_archival.txt` file, expanded by `git archive` via `export-subst`, carries the describe output that `setuptools-scm` would otherwise have to ask `git` for. The archival file deliberately omits `ref-names`. Recording it would make the content of an archive -- and therefore its checksum -- change whenever a branch that points at the archived commit is moved afterwards, which is how the equivalent tarballs of tagged releases became unstable for other projects. Describe output alone depends only on the commit and on the tags reachable from it. The archival file is not shipped in the sdist -- an sdist carries its version in its metadata, and the template is only ever expanded by `git archive`. Building pytest from a git checkout now requires `setuptools-scm >= 10.1`. - [#​9236](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9236): `pluggy>=1.6` is now required. Older pluggy versions stopped running the remaining hook wrapper teardowns once an old-style `hookwrapper` raised in its own teardown. The logging plugin's wrapper was left suspended, and when it was finalised later it detached the handler that `caplog` of a subsequent test was recording through, so that test saw no records. ##### Contributor-facing changes - [#​14813](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14813): Added a systematic coverage matrix for assertion rewriting. - [#​14921](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14921): Added scripts/diff-assert-rewrite.py, which diffs the assert-rewritten form of a snippet between the plain source, this checkout and released pytest versions. - [#​15190](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15190): Fixed the documentation build with Pluggy 1.7 by ignoring a reference to its undocumented `DistFacade` compatibility class. ##### Miscellaneous internal changes - [#​13888](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13888): `FixtureRequest.node ` is now explicitly annotated as returning `Any`, so strict pyright no longer reports it as `Unknown`. The return type stays deliberately broad, see `13888`. - [#​14758](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14758): Internal node ids (the `::`-separated strings identifying collected items, e.g. `path/to/test_file.py::TestClass::test_method[param]`) are now represented internally by a single structured `~_pytest.nodeid.NodeId` dataclass instead of being repeatedly re-parsed as plain strings. The public `nodeid: str` attribute on nodes and reports is unchanged and remains fully backward compatible for plugins.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/ruff (ruff)</summary>

### [`v0.17.4`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0174)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/compare/0.17.3...0.17.4)

Released on 2026-11-05.

##### Preview features

- \[`flake8-logging-format`] Avoid behavior changes and syntax errors in fixes (`G004`) ([#​27419](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27419))
- \[`security`] Implement `tarfile-ignore-zeros-true` ([#​28680](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28680))

##### Bug fixes

- Accept a bare raise before a semicolon ([#​29761](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29761))
- Allow match identifiers after a semicolon ([#​29760](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29760))
- Fix panic on BOM-prefixed files in diagnostic renderer ([#​30017](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30017))
- \[`flake8-simplify`] Report collapsible `elif` clauses after a multi-statement `if` branch (`SIM102`) ([#​29814](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29814))

##### Rule changes

- Show more nonprinting characters in diagnostic fix diffs ([#​30062](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30062))

##### Performance

- Coalesce source slices when formatting attributes ([#​29841](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29841))
- Collect return statements with a statement-only visitor ([#​29911](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29911))
- \[`pyflakes`] Defer value comparisons for repeated dictionary keys (`F601`, `F602`) ([#​29739](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29739))
- Format node fields directly when comment handling is unnecessary ([#​29853](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29853))
- Reduce formatter source-slice overhead ([#​29855](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29855))
- Reuse a callee's qualified name across lint rules ([#​29916](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29916))
- Skip invalid string character checks when the source contains none ([#​29883](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29883))
- Use a Bloom filter for formatter comment lookups ([#​29852](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29852))
- Use a concrete buffer for ordinary writes ([#​29819](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29819))

##### CLI

- Give `NO_COLOR` precedence in Ruff and ty diagnostics ([#​29898](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29898))
- Honor `CLICOLOR=0` in Ruff and ty diagnostics ([#​29910](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29910))

##### Documentation

- Correct the documented `version` and `src` defaults for `ruff-action` ([#​29880](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29880))
- \[`flake8-bugbear`] Make `B014` example error out-of-the-box ([#​29941](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29941))
- \[`flake8-no-pep420`] Document preview behavior (`INP001`) ([#​29764](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29764))
- \[`isort`] Expand `I001` documentation ([#​29843](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29843))

##### Other changes

- \[syntax-errors] Extend `__debug__` write check to attribute targets ([#​27908](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27908))

Released on 2026-11-12.

##### Preview features

- Redirect renamed rules ([#​30081](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30081))
- \[`flake8-async`] Implement `pytest-raises-exception-group` (`ASYNC401`) ([#​28772](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28772))
- \[`flake8-logging-format`] Mark `G004` fix as unsafe ([#​30087](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30087))
- \[`pylint`] Implement `no-method-argument` (`PLE0211`) ([#​29748](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29748))
- \[`refurb`] Do not offer fix when `write` is nested in an expression (`FURB103`) ([#​29789](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29789))
- \[`ruff`] Add `renamed-rule` (`RUF202`) ([#​30079](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30079))
- \[`ruff`] Expand `redirected-noqa` to other suppression comments (`RUF101`) ([#​30078](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30078))

##### Bug fixes

- Avoid crashing when Ruff logs to a closed stderr pipe ([#​30209](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30209))
- Fix fixes that add or remove a keyword argument with a parenthesized value ([#​30189](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30189))
- \[`flake8-import-conventions`] Avoid shadowing names when fixing import aliases (`ICN001`) ([#​30035](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30035))
- \[`flake8-bugbear`] Fix `B010` autofix for parenthesized `setattr` calls ([#​30168](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30168))
- \[`flake8-pyi`] Fix `PYI034` autofix for parenthesized `self` annotations ([#​30173](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30173))
- \[`pyupgrade`] Fix `UP031` duplicating closing parentheses around the format string ([#​30172](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30172))

##### Rule changes

body:
Shadow of the two GitHub arm64 legs on our own native arm64 runner. Nothing GitHub does changes, and nothing here can fail a release or the stable gate.

- `release-arm64.yml` (tag push): builds the arm64 assets the way `release-linux-arm64.yml` does, publishes nothing, and compares them with the copies GitHub appends (`packaging/compare-arch-build.sh`: package metadata, file lists with modes and link targets, signatures, archive contents).
- `install-matrix-arm64.yml` (dispatched by `publish.yml` beside the other two matrices): the same four arm64 install shards.
- Both are their own workflows so a queued or slow arm64 job can never hold the publish run or the install-matrix run the stable gate reads. Every step that can fail is continue-on-error; the verdict is the `SHADOW-VERDICT` line.

Proved on a throwaway repo against the current candidates (dreame-valetudo v0.3.0-rc.49, whiskerless v0.2.0-rc.76): both builds `VERDICT agree` with GitHub's assets; install shards all pass except dreame-valetudo's bottle-pour, because the tap carries no bottle for rc.49 (GitHub's own rc.49 matrix never reached its shards: its wait found the macOS .pkg missing).

The flip (the upload replaces the compare, GitHub's copies go) is a later PR once a real release candidate shows both agree.

Shadow of GitHub's `ci-macos.yml` and `formula-macos.yml` on our own Mac: macOS 15 (the floor) and the newest macOS, each in its own VM. Nothing GitHub does changes.

- `macos.yml` runs on every push to every branch, keyed per commit like GitHub's (cancelled only on Renovate branches), with the same `macos-scope.sh` skip for Linux-only Renovate branches. No pull_request trigger, so a fork's code never runs on these machines.
- The Homebrew formula smoke runs first, while the VM is as clean as a user's Mac, then the native tests, shellcheck and the release-script tests.
- Every check is continue-on-error; the verdict is the `SHADOW-VERDICT tier=... ci=... formula=...` line. The one step allowed to fail the job is the Python setup, so nothing pip-installs into the image's own interpreter.
- setup-python's macOS build expects GitHub's tool cache path and an admin runner user; the job provides the path and hands the framework it installs to the job user between the two attempts.

On this branch both VMs ran green: SHADOW-VERDICT ci=success formula=success on floor and current.

The switch (GitHub's copies go, the gates read this) is a later PR after about a week of agreement.

body:
Closes #280

Large diff: mostly deletions. The GitHub CI workflows go, the vendored helpers that bridged to them are replaced by the project-rules v0.3.0 re-vendor, and their invariant tests go with them.

**Contributing.** Issues and pull requests go to Forgejo, where anyone can sign in with a GitHub account; the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror. CONTRIBUTING describes the AGit flow (`git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main -o topic=…`). CI does not run on a pull request sent that way: the runners are trusted with release credentials. A maintainer reads the change and opens it again from a branch here, which runs the whole suite.

**CI on our own runners only.**
- `macos.yml` is the macOS gate, on macOS 15 and the newest macOS. It runs on push to every branch, never on pull_request, and swallows no failures (only the setup-python fallback stays tolerated).
- Its two jobs replace `CI / macos (pull_request)` as required checks on `main`: `macOS / macOS floor (macos-15-vm) (push)` and `macOS / macOS current (macos-27-vm) (push)`. Branch protection is updated when this merges.
- `ci.yml` loses the `macos` job that waited on GitHub's run.
- The release and prerelease `mirror-gate` becomes `macos-gate`. It runs `check-forgejo-ci.sh <sha> macos.yml` with no credential, and passes only a run whose every job succeeded, so a scoped-out Renovate run cannot qualify a cut.
- The candidate gate asks Forgejo only. It reads `install-matrix.yml` (amd64) and refuses to trust a shadow matrix: `install-matrix-arm64.yml` swallows its own failures, so a test now fails if it is ever listed in `INSTALL_MATRIX_WORKFLOWS`.
- Deleted: `.github/workflows/ci-pr.yml`, `ci-macos.yml`, `formula-macos.yml` and `retry-infra-failures.yml`. With them go the vendored `check-mirror-ci.sh`, `triage-infra-failure.py`, `forgejo-preflight.sh` and their tests.
- Docs (`docs/design/ci-split.md`, `packaging/README.md`) and invariant tests are rewritten to match. The new tests check that `macos.yml` never runs on pull_request, swallows nothing and covers both macOS legs. They also check that the release gate requires a fully green run on the exact commit, and that the candidate gate lists every install-matrix workflow.

**Release side, until the release-in-house PR lands.**
- The re-vendor removes `forgejo-preflight.sh`, so this PR deletes its step from the GitHub release workflows that remain. Its only reader was the infra-retry workflow, which goes too.
- The candidate gate now reads Forgejo only and cannot see GitHub's macOS and arm64 install legs. So `release.yml` refuses a stable cut while `.github/workflows/install-matrix.yml` exists; a test pins that refusal. Prereleases are unaffected.
- The release-in-house PR moves those legs here and removes both the file and the refusal.

**Also tightened.**
- The AGit trust-gate test covers every job of a pull-request workflow, with recorded exceptions, not only the jobs that already had a head-repository check.
- The ref check on the gated macOS workflow is case-insensitive, so a script reading `$GITHUB_REF` is caught too.

Checks run here: ruff, mypy, the full pytest suite, `tests/release/*.sh`, `shellcheck-all.sh`. cx review raised the release-side gaps above (fixed by the preflight removal and the refusal); qx reviewed the follow-ups.

body:
Forgejo treats an AGit pull request (pushed to `refs/for/main`, no fork needed) as untrusted and holds its runs for approval, but its payload reports this repository as the head (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), so the existing fork gate let it through. When a maintainer acts on an outsider's PR (reopen), Forgejo 17 runs this branch's workflows, with secrets, against the PR's commit (services/actions/trust.go). Outside contributors are about to be able to sign in with GitHub and open AGit PRs, so the gate now also requires `github.event.pull_request.flow == 0`.

Proof (throwaway SisyphusMD/agit-guard-proof-20261116): an AGit PR's payload has `flow=1` and head repo = base repo, and the gated job was skipped (run 37485); a branch PR has `flow=0` and the gated job ran (run 37486).

Outside PRs get CI when a maintainer, after reading the diff, pushes the head to a branch here.

The shellcheck job stays open to every PR by design (it reads scripts, never executes them, and references no secret). New test `test_trust_gates_also_exclude_agit_pull_requests` fails on the old ci.yml (python, python-floor, build, integration, macos) and passes now.

`DustBuilder forms / verify` has failed on every run since 2026-10-28: each weekly scheduled run, and every pull request that touches the forms workflow or its watched files (#275 changes the workflow file, so its path filter matches). The cause is upstream. builder.dontvacuum.me still resolves (139.162.132.106) and the host answers ping, but ports 80 and 443 refuse connections from outside networks too. dontvacuum.me itself is up and still links the builder, and Valetudo's docs still point at it, so it has not moved. Before this change, `verify-forms` reported a page it could not fetch as a failed comparison, the same exit 1 as a changed form.

Now each page is a match, a change, or could not be fetched:
- Any fetched page that differs from its golden still exits 1 and fails the job, even when other pages are unreachable.
- When nothing differed but a page could not be fetched, `verify-forms` exits 3. The workflow turns that into a warning ("DustBuilder could not be reached, so its forms were not checked") and does not advance the verified-on date. The date the tool shows as last verified therefore keeps reflecting the last full match.

The new tests reject:
- an all-fetches-failed run reported as anything but "unreachable";
- a changed form hidden behind an unreachable page;
- the exit-code mapping;
- the stamp step running on anything but a full match.

9 of them fail against main's code.

No sibling change: whiskerless has no DustBuilder.

title: Stage 1 and build guidance still use the retired DustBuilder

body:
Closes #277

Large diff: this replaces the retired DustBuilder with Dustfab in one piece. `dustbuilder.py` (342 lines) is deleted and `dustfab.py` replaces it, and the goldens are regenerated. The stage 1 fetch, the image checklist, the FEL package watcher and the drift check all read the same per-model Dustfab URLs, so landing only part of the port leaves fresh installs broken or the tool pointing at a dead host.

**Trigger.** `builder.dontvacuum.me` has refused connections since late October. `fetch` downloaded the stage 1 FEL payload from it, so every fresh install died before recon. Valetudo's Dreame guide now sends fastboot users to Dustfab (`fab.valetudo.cloud`). The weekly `DustBuilder forms` check has been red since 10/28 for the same reason, and that holds every PR that touches its workflow.

**What happens now**
- `fetch` downloads the model's own recon package from `/robot/<brand>/<code>/fel/recon` and checks it against a per-model SHA-256 pin before extracting it. Mova models live under `mova`.
  - All 13 pins were re-taken today. Dustfab rebuilt the shared `payload.bin` on 10/27 (still dustversion `2026.10.00`), so every pin from the original 10/26 port would have refused the download. The FSBL digests are unchanged.
  - `sunxi-fel` still loads `fsbl.bin` and `payload.bin`. The bundled `valetudo-helper-felroot-amd64` runs only on amd64 Linux, so the tool does not use it.
- Recon selects each slice with `oem stage<n>` before `get_staged`, the order the current guide uses.
- The image step walks through Dustfab's build form (pasted `authorized_keys`, `outputFormat=fel`, no voucher, e-mail or affidavit) and its per-model check page. It stages Dustfab's `.tar.gz` FEL package once the download has settled. A build that carries `dtbo.img` is refused before any write, because the tool does not flash `dtbo` yet.
- The `Dustfab forms` workflow (renamed from `dustbuilder-forms.yml`) compares every build page, check page and brand listing with its golden. It also fetches one recon package per distinct pin, three in all because Dustfab rate-limits recon downloads, and fails when a digest moves.
- `verify-forms` exits 3 when Dustfab never answered (curl 6/7/28/35) and nothing fetched differed. The workflow turns that into a warning. An HTTP error, an empty page or a changed page still fails. This folds in the useful half of #276.
- The contract markers follow the current Supported Robots text. Valetudo replaced the look-alike name notes with serial prefixes and reworded the Heat SSH fix in October, which left 9 markers stale.
- The shipped "last verified" date is written by the release and prerelease gates, which run the same check. Branch protection refuses the old bot commit to main.

**What the tests reject**
- a stage 1 package whose digest differs from its pin, with three empty downloads counted as a failure;
- an unreachable host reported as a changed page, and an error page reported as unreachable;
- a changed page hidden behind an unreachable one;
- the verify-forms exit-code mapping;
- the workflow failing on exit 3 or passing on 1;
- a release tag job that drops or invents the verified-on stamp.

**Checked live on 2026-11-16**
- `verify-forms` matched all 29 Dustfab pages and the 3 sampled packages.
- `verify_valetudo_contract` against Valetudo `27d79e8` reported all 13 fastboot contracts matching.

**Not proven**
- No robot has run this branch.
- The 10/27 payload has not been FEL-booted through `sunxi-fel` or answered `oem stage<n>` / `get_staged` from this tool.
- No real Dustfab build has gone through the image watcher.
- No macOS run. CI cannot touch hardware; a bench run is the proof.

**Sibling.** whiskerless has no DustBuilder or Dustfab dependency. Its release workflows have no forms stamp because there is no external form to verify, so there is nothing to converge.

title: Run CI on this project's own runners only

body:
Every release asset is still built or tested on GitHub-hosted runners: the signed `.pkg`, the Homebrew bottles, the arm64 Linux set and the macOS and arm64 install legs. This project now has its own macOS 15, newest-macOS and arm64 runners, so all of that can move in-house and GitHub only receives the release.

- `release-macos.yml` and `bottles.yml` move to `.forgejo/workflows/`. The `.pkg` is built, signed, notarized and stapled on the macOS 15 VM and tested again on the newest-macOS VM. Bottles are built for macOS 15, Linux amd64 and Linux arm64. Each workflow uploads to all three releases (public Forgejo, NAS, GitHub).
- `release-arm64.yml` becomes the arm64 publisher. Its compare-with-GitHub shadow goes, and so does `.github/workflows/release-linux-arm64.yml`.
- `install-matrix.yml` covers Linux amd64, Linux arm64 and macOS in one run. `install-matrix-arm64.yml` and the GitHub install matrix go, along with `publish.yml`'s GitHub dispatch.
- The NAS bridge jobs (`nas-bridge`, `nas-bottles`) go, because every producer reaches the NAS directly. `reconcile` waits for the `.pkg` and the arm64 set before healing.
- The Apple signing secrets move to Forgejo org secrets.

Follows the CI-side change in #280.

body:
Closes #281

Large diff: moving four release workflows from `.github` to `.forgejo` (or merging them in), plus the tests and docs that pin them, can't be split without leaving a release path half on GitHub.

## What changes
- `release-macos.yml` and `bottles.yml` move to Forgejo. The `.pkg` is built, signed, notarized and stapled on macos-15-vm, then tested on macos-27-vm. Bottles build on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-26.04-arm and macos-15-vm. Each uploads straight to the Forgejo, NAS and GitHub releases. The nas-pkg and nas-bottles bridges are gone.
- `release-arm64.yml` is now the real arm64 publisher. `release-linux-arm64.yml`, the shadow and `compare-arch-build.sh` are deleted.
- One `install-matrix.yml` covers amd64, arm64 and both macOS VMs (pkg/spctl, bottle pour, uvx). The GitHub install matrix, `install-matrix-arm64.yml` and the GitHub dispatch are deleted.
- reconcile waits until the .pkg and arm64 set are on both the public Forgejo and the NAS.
- The stable-cut refusal step and its test are removed. `.github/workflows` is empty, and a test keeps it that way.
- Deviation, already approved: the .pkg and bottles stay as their own workflows instead of being folded into publish.yml.
- All eight `MACOS_*` secrets are present as Forgejo org secrets.

## Proof (private proof repo; build and verify only, no uploads)
- Bottles: all three legs. Keg lists and tabs are identical to the GitHub-built bottles (tab differences are only Homebrew version drift).
- Unsigned .pkg: payload files and per-binary minimum macOS are identical to the GitHub-built .pkg.
- macOS install legs on macos-15-vm and macos-27-vm: spctl accepts the published pkg as notarized, the bottle pours and uvx works, on two runs back to back.
- Signed .pkg, run 37945 (2 jobs): built, signed, notarized (Accepted) and stapled on macos-15-vm twice in a row. `stapler validate` OK, `spctl -a -t install` accepted as Notarized Developer ID, payload files IDENTICAL to the GitHub-built pkg (16 entries), and minimum macOS per binary IDENTICAL.

- Signing needed one change on the runner side: each job now sets the keychain search list and default (`list-keychains -d user -s`, `default-keychain -d user -s`), since every job starts with neither. A test pins both lines.

## Checks
ruff, mypy, pytest with coverage floors, shellcheck, actionlint and doc links all pass locally. Codex review found nothing.

##### v8 - What's new

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> actions/download-artifact\@​v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

##### Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in `actions/upload-artifact`, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the `Content-Type` header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new `skip-decompress` parameter to `true`.

##### Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the `digest-mismatch` parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to `error` which will fail the workflow run.

##### ESM

To support new versions of the @​actions/\* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

##### What's Changed

- Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by [@​danwkennedy](https://github.com/danwkennedy) in [#​460](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/460)

##### What's Changed

- BREAKING fix: inconsistent path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID by [@​GrantBirki](https://github.com/GrantBirki) in [#​416](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/416)

##### v5.0.0

##### 🚨 Breaking Change

This release fixes an inconsistency in path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID. **If you're downloading single artifacts by ID, the output path may change.**

##### What Changed

Previously, **single artifact downloads** behaved differently depending on how you specified the artifact:

- **By name**: `name: my-artifact` → extracted to `path/` (direct)
- **By ID**: `artifact-ids: 12345` → extracted to `path/my-artifact/` (nested)

Now both methods are consistent:

- **By name**: `name: my-artifact` → extracted to `path/` (unchanged)
- **By ID**: `artifact-ids: 12345` → extracted to `path/` (fixed - now direct)

##### Migration Guide

##### ✅ No Action Needed If:

- You download artifacts by **name**
- You download **multiple** artifacts by ID
- You already use `merge-multiple: true` as a workaround

##### ⚠️ Action Required If:

You download **single artifacts by ID** and your workflows expect the nested directory structure.

**Before v5 (nested structure):**

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    artifact-ids: 12345
    path: dist

# Files were in: dist/my-artifact/
```

> Where `my-artifact` is the name of the artifact you previously uploaded

**To maintain old behavior (if needed):**

```yaml
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
  with:
    artifact-ids: 12345
    path: dist/my-artifact  # Explicitly specify the nested path
```

##### What's Changed

The release of upload-artifact\@​v4 and download-artifact\@​v4 are major changes to the backend architecture of Artifacts. They have numerous performance and behavioral improvements.

ℹ️ However, this is a major update that includes breaking changes. Artifacts created with versions v3 and below are not compatible with the v4 actions. Uploads and downloads *must* use the same major actions versions. There are also key differences from previous versions that may require updates to your workflows.

For more information, please see:

1. The [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2023-12-14-github-actions-artifacts-v4-is-now-generally-available/) post.
2. The [migration documentation](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md).
3. As well as the underlying npm package, [@​actions/artifact](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/tree/main/packages/artifact) documentation.

##### Breaking Changes

1. download-artifact\@​v4+ is not currently supported on GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) yet. If you are on GHES, you must use [v3](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v3) (Node 16) or [v3-node20](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v3-node20) (Node 20).
2. On self hosted runners, additional [firewall rules](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/tree/main/packages/artifact#breaking-changes) may be required.
3. Downloading artifacts that were created from `action/upload-artifact@v3` and below are not supported.

For assistance with breaking changes, see [MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md).

##### Improvements

1. Downloads are significantly faster, upwards of 90% improvement in worst case scenarios.
2. Artifacts can be downloaded from other workflow runs and repositories when supplied with a PAT.

##### Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new `archive` parameter to `false` to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. head: refs/pull/284/head
title: chore(deps): update github artifact actions (major) - autoclosed

body:
Renovate opened a major bump of `actions/upload-artifact` (v3.2.2 -> v7.0.2) and `actions/download-artifact` (v3.1.0 -> v8.0.2). It passes CI, but it would break the release: v4 and later throw `GHESNotSupportedError` on any server whose `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` is not github.com, which is every Forgejo run. `bottles.yml` and `release-macos.yml` pass the bottles and the signed `.pkg` between jobs through these actions, and PR CI never runs either workflow.

Plan: a `packageRules` entry that holds both actions below v4, so Renovate stops proposing the bump and closes the open PR. The held PR stays unmerged until then.

comments.body: PR #286 adds the Renovate hold (`<4`) and a test pinning the workflow lines to v3; CI green, READY for merge. #284 left unmerged; Renovate should close it after #286 lands.

title: Hold the artifact actions on v3 (v4+ refuses Forgejo)

body:
Closes #285

Renovate PR #284 bumps `actions/upload-artifact` to v7 and `actions/download-artifact` to v8. Its CI is green, but it would break the next release: v4 and later throw `GHESNotSupportedError` whenever `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` is not github.com (read in the v7.0.2 dist, `isGhes()`), which is every Forgejo run. `bottles.yml` and `release-macos.yml` hand the bottles and the signed `.pkg` between jobs through these actions, and neither runs on a pull request.

- `.renovaterc.json`: a rule holds both actions at `<4`. Renovate should then close #284 on its next run.
- A test pins both halves: every artifact step's version comment says v3, and the Renovate ceiling exists. It fails on a v7 line (checked).

Reviewed with `qx review`; the findings that held up are applied.
head: refs/pull/286/head
title: ci: hold the artifact actions below v4 (v4+ refuses Forgejo)

body:
The release path still uses `actions/upload-artifact` v3.2.2 and `actions/download-artifact` v3.1.0 (held there by #285 because GitHub's v4+ throws `GHESNotSupportedError` off github.com). Forgejo maintains forks with that check removed: `code.forgejo.org/forgejo/upload-artifact` and `code.forgejo.org/forgejo/download-artifact`.

Plan (Cody, 2026-11-17): switch `bottles.yml` and `release-macos.yml` to the forks, pinned by SHA with full `https://code.forgejo.org/...` URLs (upload `v5`, download `v7`, a v4+ protocol pair); replace the v3 pin test with one that pins the forks and forbids `actions/upload-artifact` / `actions/download-artifact` at any version; drop the Renovate `<4` hold and let Renovate track the forks (forgejo-tags datasource, held for hand review). Proven in a private proof repo with every publish step removed, on every runner label, before merge.

comments.body: PR #288 (head 76373d7). Picked upload v5 + download v7: smoke run 38150 on a private proof repo passed upload, by-name download (own and cross-label), sha256 match and missing-artifact failure on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-26.04-arm, macos-15-vm and macos-27-vm. Release-path proof runs in progress.

title: Move the artifact actions to the Forgejo forks

body:
Closes #287

Replaces the v3 hold from #286: `bottles.yml` and `release-macos.yml` now use Forgejo's forks, pinned by commit with full URLs.

- `https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/upload-artifact@cb8afe72… # v5` and `https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/download-artifact@769f9704… # v7`. Only the forks' bare major tags carry Forgejo's GHES-check removal (the upstream `vX.Y.Z` tags mirrored beside them still refuse Forgejo), so the comment is the major tag. Upload `branch-v6` exists but is untagged, so v5 is the newest upload. v5 and v7 are both v4+ protocol (`@actions/artifact` 4 and 5).
- Workflow steps unchanged otherwise: artifact names are already unique per run, downloads are by name into the same `path:` (the by-name extraction is identical), and the three per-leg `continue-on-error` downloads still fail softly on a missing leg.
- The pin test now requires the fork URL, a 40-char SHA and a bare major tag on every artifact line, one version of each across both workflows, and fails on `actions/upload-artifact` / `actions/download-artifact` at any version.
- Renovate: the `<4` hold is gone. The forks are tracked through `forgejo-tags` on code.forgejo.org (Renovate 44.251.0 local dry run: both found at v5/v7; with v4 pins it proposes v5/v7 at the patched SHAs on one `renovate/forgejo-artifact-actions` branch). Allowed versions are bare major tags only, grouped, majors not split from digests, and never automerged, with a PR note that a release-path proof run is the gate.

Proof (private throwaway repo, every publish step removed, nothing published): see the comment below once the runs finish.

comments.body:
Proof, private throwaway repo SisyphusMD/ci-artifact-proof-20261117 (tag v0.3.0-rc.51 tree + this PR's two workflows; triggers, tag checkout and every publish step removed; artifact `uses:` lines byte-identical to this PR). Nothing published.

- Smoke 38150: upload v5 + download v7 on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-26.04-arm, macos-15-vm, macos-27-vm. Own and cross-label downloads sha256-OK, a missing name fails (so the per-leg `continue-on-error` still works).
- release-macos 38165: macos-15-vm built, signed, notarized (Accepted), stapled and uploaded `pkg-arm64`. macos-27-vm downloaded it to `.` and test-macos-package passed (spctl: Notarized Developer ID). ubuntu-latest downloaded it to `pkgs/`. sha256 a8d20f47… is the same in all three jobs.
- bottles 38178: all three legs uploaded `bottle-<label>`, and the publish job downloaded all three into `bottles/`; every sha256 matches its manifest. A proof job on each label downloaded its own leg, pointed root_url at it, ran `brew bottle --merge --write` into the tap formula, and `brew install` POURED it: arm64_sequoia, x86_64_linux and arm64_linux all printed `dreame-valetudo 0.3.0-rc.51`.

body:
The `compare model and rooting contracts with official Valetudo` step in `dustfab-forms.yml` runs:

    git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/Hypfer/Valetudo.git /tmp/upstream-valetudo

Why it is fragile:

1. **One attempt.** A single network blip or GitHub hiccup fails the weekly run (and any pull request touching the contract files) red, with nothing wrong in either repository. The Dustfab step next to it already treats "could not reach the site" as a warning for this reason.
2. **No time bound.** A stalled connection holds the runner until the job's own timeout.
3. **The whole tree.** The verifier reads three paths (`backend/lib/robots/dreame`, `docs/pages/general/supported-robots.md`, `docs/pages/installation/dreame.md`), but the step downloads every file of the default branch.

Proposed fix: a blobless sparse clone of only `backend/lib/robots/dreame` and `docs/pages`, bounded by `timeout`, retried up to three times with a fresh directory each time, and still failing the job if every attempt fails (a contract check that silently skips is worse than a red run). The clone stays on the upstream default branch on purpose: the check exists to notice upstream drift.

comments.body: Merged in #293 at 86b5de1. Dustfab contract verification passed with the sparse checkout, and tests cover recovery after transient failures and final failure after all attempts.

title: Valetudo contract check: the upstream clone is fragile

The trust-gate test itself already checks every `pull_request` job (a job with no `if:` fails it), so it is unchanged.
- **#290.** Every checkout in `publish.yml` and `prune-rcs.yml` sets `persist-credentials: false`. No job there pushes this repository; the two Homebrew tap jobs clone and push another repository with their own explicit header, which never used the persisted one. New test: every checkout in both workflows disclaims the token (it fails on main, naming six jobs); the prune-dispatch test now expects the key.
- **#292.** The Valetudo contract step now does a blobless sparse clone of only `backend/lib/robots/dreame` and `docs/pages`, under `timeout 300`, up to three tries, and still fails the job after the third. New tests run the step itself with git stubbed: two transient failures then success runs the verifier once; three failures exit 1 without running it. Both fail on main's step.

Closes #289
Closes #290
Closes #291
Closes #292

comments.body:
<!-- ai-review -->
**AI review** of `f7d56bccb3`: The PR restructures Homebrew tap publishing to use PR-based submission with credential isolation, which is a sound security improvement. The main structural changes (render/submit split, reusable workflow, wait-for-land logic) are well-designed. One earlier finding is resolved by the code's actual behavior; one remains unverifiable from the diff; and the reusable workflow may be missing a required secrets declaration for Forgejo's workflow_call.

### Open

- **F1** (suggestion, `packaging/update-tap.sh:167`) Template path `$work/src/packaging/homebrew/` likely does not exist in the sdist: The finding concerns a path in `packaging/update-tap.sh` that is not present in this PR's diff, so I cannot confirm or deny it from the diff alone. If the path `$work/src/packaging/homebrew/${formula}.rb` is still in the script and `$work` is the sdist extraction root, the `src/` prefix would not match the actual tree (the project's `src/` layout applies to the Python package; `packaging/` sits at the repo root). Please verify with `tar tzf dist/*.tar.gz | grep homebrew` and confirm the path resolves at release time. If the path was corrected in a prior push, mark this resolved.
- **F3** (suggestion, `.forgejo/workflows/submit-tap-formula.yml:5`) `workflow_call` trigger does not declare `secrets`, so `secrets.tap-token` may be empty at runtime: The reusable workflow uses `${{ secrets.tap-token }}` (line 47) and the callers pass it via `secrets: tap-token: …`, but the `on.workflow_call` block declares only `inputs`—no `secrets:` section. In GitHub Actions (and Forgejo's Actions implementation, which follows the same schema), a reusable workflow cannot read a secret unless it is declared under `on.workflow_call.secrets`. Without the declaration the `secrets` context in the called workflow is empty, `TOKEN` would be blank, and the PR-creation step would fail at the first real release. The existing test (`test_tap_publisher_isolates_credentials_and_waits_for_landed_formulae`) asserts `set(…["workflow_call"]) == {"inputs"}`, which would need updating. Add:
```yaml
    secrets:
      tap-token:
        required: true
```
under `on.workflow_call`, and update the test assertion to `{"inputs", "secrets"}`. If Forgejo's current implementation passes all org/repo secrets implicitly without a declaration, please confirm that with a dry-run dispatch and note it in a comment so the next reader doesn't hit the same question.

### Withdrawn

- **F2** (suggestion, `.forgejo/workflows/submit-tap-formula.yml:53`) Non-pending, non-merged PR states silently succeed without files landing: On re-examination, the `jq -er 'select(.state == "pending" or .state == "landed" or .state == "superseded")'` expression produces no output for any other state (e.g. "closed"), causing jq to exit with code 4. Combined with `set -euo pipefail`, the step fails immediately. Unknown terminal states are therefore caught and the job does not silently succeed. The finding was incorrect.
  - Reviewer: Withdrawn: `jq -er` with a `select` that matches nothing exits non-zero (code 4), and `set -euo pipefail` propagates that as a step failure. Unknown states like "closed" do not silently pass.
